newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN SHARE TRADE BOOSTED BY UPBEAT WALL ST CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN SHARE TRADE BOOSTED BY UPBEAT WALL ST CLOSE.

text.p: German IBIS DAX index advanced over one percent in pre-bourse electronic trade on Tuesday, heartened by an upbeat close on Wall Street overnight and the stable dollar against the mark.
By 0722 GMT the IBIS DAX index stood at 4,374.71 points, up 41.56 points, while the September DAX future contract was also in positive territory, up 59.5 points at 4,390 points.
"Volumes are very thin today, and I reckon we will probably see fairly strong resistance at around 4,400 points," a Frankfurt trader said.
The way things have gone on the DAX recently, everything is possible on the upside, the dealer said, but the more likely scenario was a trading range of between 4,370 and 4,390 points.
The German share market saw its lowest volumes since mid-June on Monday, and the dealer said there was no reason to expect a much different situation on Tuesday.
"Buying interest is very selective this morning," the trader said.
Among the shares favoured during electronic trade was the retailer Karstadt AG, which was top gainer pre-bourse, up 3.51 percent at 723 marks.
A spokesman for the Schickedanz retail group said that it planned to buy stakes in Karstadt held by Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank, but said its aim was not to take over the firm.
The move was viewed positively by the markets.
Other shares in the news included Henkel KgAA which was up 3.10 marks, or 3.08 percent, at 103.70 marks after it released interim results.
Henkel's pretax profit rose 10 percent to 438 million marks from 397 million in the first half of 1997, while group sales rose to 9.784 billion marks from 8.039 billion marks.

Otherwise the main drivers behind the IBIS DAX index were the banks. Bankgesellschaft Berlin was up 2.77 percent at 50 marks, Deutsche Bank was up 1.52 percent at 120.35 marks and Dresdner Bank was up 1.58 percent at 82.80 marks.
